title: Finance Manager (Daily Reporting)
description:
Full time, 40 hours a week, spread across 7 days. Remote, based in the Philippines. Reports to the CEO.



We are a 24/7 business. That is why the week is 7 days and not 5. The hours are normal, the rhythm is not.

We are a two entity, two market, inventory heavy DTC beauty business running on Shopify and Amazon with China direct and 3PL fulfilment. Revenue is not our problem. Visibility is.



We need a qualified accountant who turns a messy, cross border operation into a small set of numbers we can look at every single day and trust. Not a month end role. Not a board deck role. A daily discipline role.



The rhythm is the point: a report lands every morning, seven days a week, including weekends and holidays. We spend money on ads every day, so we need to see profit and cash every day. Weekends are when problems hide.

The Philippines time zone is a deliberate advantage here. You work your morning, the previous European day has just closed, and your pack is in Slack before Amsterdam opens.



You will work alongside our existing external accounting partners (a US accounting firm, Dutch bookkeepers and a cross border accountant) rather than replacing them. They handle statutory and compliance. You own management reporting.



The daily rhythm

Every day, 7 days a week, delivered by 13:00 PHT (around 07:00 CET):

• Cash position across all bank accounts and both entities

• Yesterday’s revenue, gross profit and ad spend by market and channel

• Blended MER and contribution margin after ad spend

• Refunds, chargebacks and payment provider reserve movements

• Any red flag, called out in one line at the top

Weekend versions can be a lighter, largely templated snapshot, but they land.

Every Monday:

• Full management P&L for the prior week

• Contribution margin by SKU, channel and market

• Inventory position and stock cover in weeks

• Rolling 13 week cash flow forecast, updated

• KPI pack for the founding team

Every month:

• Consolidated cross border P&L (NL and US) and balance sheet review

• Variance against plan, with commentary on the why

• Reconciliation sign off across Shopify, Amazon, payment providers, 3PL and the ledger

What You’ll Own Beyond the Reporting

• Cash forecasting: the rolling 13 week forecast, including inventory and purchase order cash planning against production lead times

• Unit economics: true landed COGS per SKU (freight, duty, fulfilment), and contribution margin by SKU, channel, market and cohort

• Channel P&Ls: Shopify DACH, Shopify US, Amazon US, comparable and reconciled

• Payment risk monitoring: reserves, rolling reserves and chargeback exposure

• FX exposure across EUR, USD and PHP

• Invoice verification: supplier and 3PL invoices checked against contracted terms

• Automation: templates, defined metrics, connected data sources. If the daily pack takes two hours by month three, something is wrong



What We’re Looking For

• Philippine CPA, or an equivalent qualification with a strong practical track record

• 4+ years in accounting or finance, including hands on management reporting

• Ecommerce or inventory based business experience

• Advanced Excel or Google Sheets. You have built cash flow models yourself

• Comfortable reconciling data from Shopify, Amazon Seller Central, payment gateways and 3PL reports

• Multi currency and multi entity experience

title: Supply Chain Manager
description:
We are a fast growing DTC skincare brand selling in 8 countries, producing direct with manufacturers in China and fulfilling through a 3PL and Amazon FBA. We are looking for a Supply Chain Manager to own everything from the factory to the warehouse shelf.



Full time. Owns production, inbound logistics, stock planning and Amazon inbound. Reports to the COO.



What You Own

-The suppliers. You are the single point of contact with our manufacturers in China. Pricing, production orders, cargo ready dates, and pushing for a partial shipment when we need stock sooner. You come back with a date, not with a promise to check.

-The stock. You know our stock level per SKU per market without being asked, and you reorder before anything runs out. If a SKU will go out of stock inside its own lead time, we hear it from you first. You also keep the 3PL inventory records right, per SKU code, and you flag it when their numbers and ours do not agree.

-Quality control. You agree the inspection date with the supplier, coordinate with our QC firm, and get the inspection booked in time to cover a meaningful part of the order rather than the last carton.

-Barcodes and labelling. The right barcode on the right product, checked on the line before production runs. A wrong barcode caught after 50,000 units are sealed is a failure of this role.

-Compliance and documentation. Lab testing for each market, certification, ingredient and claim documents, UPC registration, and checking packaging artwork before it goes to print.

-Inbound logistics. Freight quotes and bookings, sea and air, carton and pallet planning, customs and duty, and delivery into our 3PL.

-Amazon inbound. FBA shipment plans with our 3PL, relabelling instructions, cartonization, and getting goods dispatched into the Amazon warehouse.

-New product production. From sample through to first shipment.

-Supplier invoices. You prepare and submit them with the matching order so finance can verify and pay. You do not pay them yourself.

-Reporting. Stock cover per SKU, landed cost per SKU to finance, every open production order with its date, and anything at risk, once a week without being asked.



What You Do Not Own

This is here so there is no confusion about it later.

• Individual customer orders. Ready for pickup lists, failed deliveries, returns to sender, reshipments, refunds and fraud risk orders sit with the backend order team.

• Customer service and disputes.

• Paying invoices. You prepare, finance pays.

• The Amazon account itself. Listings, pricing, advertising and account health sit elsewhere. You own what physically goes into the warehouse.

How the Role Is Judged

• Nothing sits still without us knowing it is sitting. If you are waiting on a decision, a sample or a supplier, you say so the same day.

• No stockout that was visible in advance. Lead times are known, so running out is a planning failure, not bad luck.

• You raise the problem before it reaches us from the 3PL or from a customer.

• You do not need to be chased for an update.

What We’re Looking For

• You have run production directly with manufacturers in China, not through an agent or a trading company.

• You have placed and tracked purchase orders against lead times for a physical product business, with stock cover as the number you were judged on.

• You have shipped into Amazon FBA yourself: barcodes, labelling, cartonization, inbound placement.

• Cosmetics or another regulated category, so certification, claims and ingredient documents are not new to you.

• Freight experience: quotes, bookings, customs and duty, sea and air.

• You overlap with both China and Europe in your working day.

• Full time. This role failed before as a part time arrangement and we are not repeating that.

• You work ahead of the problem rather than reacting to it.



What to Include in Your Application

• The products you ran production for, the supplier country, and the volume per month or per year.

• One FBA shipment you planned, with the units and the carton count.

• A stockout you caused or inherited, and what you changed afterwards.

• One time you pushed a supplier into a date they said was impossible, and how.

• Your time zone and your working hours.

title: Head of Paid Media
description:
We are a fast growing DTC skincare brand running around €2.4M a month in ad spend across the US and DACH. Today Google and Pinterest sit with external agencies. We want them in house. We are looking for a Head of Paid Media to own every paid channel we run and to take that work back from the agencies.



Full time. Owns all paid channels and the people on them. Reports to the founders. Compensation reflects the level of experience we are asking for.



What You’ll Do

• Own paid media across Meta, Google, TikTok, AppLovin, Pinterest and native.

• Bring the agency channels in house. Google and Pinterest are run externally today. Your job is to run them yourself or with your own buyers, at the same or better result.

• Lead the buyers on each channel and hold them to a number.

• Launch, scale and pause within agreed budgets, on your own call. We should not have to tell you what to do.

• Direct the creative strategists on what the account needs next, based on what is actually performing.

• Stay current. Media buying changes constantly and we expect you to bring the changes to us, not hear about them from us.

• Deliver a weekly report that explains performance, what you learned and what you are changing.



What We’re Looking For

• Meta: you have personally run at least €2M to €2.5M a month. €2.5M to €3M is better. This is the first thing we check.

• Google: at least €500K a month. Not advised on, not overseen. Run.

• Across all channels together, €3M to €4M a month is the level we are looking for.

• Real experience on TikTok, AppLovin and native, enough to lead those channels rather than learn them on our budget.

• You have taken a channel off an agency and run it in house before, or you can explain exactly how you would.

• You lead buyers. Hiring them, setting their targets, replacing them when needed.

• You own the number. Not the activity, the number.



What to Include in Your Application

• Your highest monthly spend on Meta, the brand, and the period. Say plainly whether you ran it yourself or managed someone who did.

• The same for Google.

• A screenshot or export from the ad platform showing that spend with the date range visible. If you cannot share it, name the company and the period so we can verify it, or give us a reference who will confirm the number.

• One channel you took in house from an agency, and what happened to the result.

 and Instagram. Most videos are around 60 to 90 seconds long.



Our videos are in Dutch, but you do not need to speak Dutch. We provide every script in both Dutch and English. It is important that you can use the English translation to fully understand the Dutch voiceover and make the visuals feel natural, relevant and easy to follow.



WHAT YOU’LL CREATE



Our ads are a mix of:



• High-quality educational AI animations

• Pixar-style AI storytelling

• Hyperrealistic AI UGC

• AI avatars

• B-roll and image-to-video



Quality is extremely important to us. We are not looking for AI slop.



Every scene should feel intentional, polished and match exactly what is being said.



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR



You should understand:



• Strong hooks and attention retention

• Direct-response advertising

• Pacing, storytelling and visual flow

• How to keep viewers watching

• How to match visuals naturally to a script

• How to create high-quality AI generations

• How to turn a script into an ad that can actually perform



You should be able to think beyond just editing and actively improve the creative.



You’ll get full access to our Higgsfield account with unlimited credits, so you can generate as much as needed to reach the right quality.



COMPENSATION



You are paid per video, with additional bonuses for winning ads.



We start with around 3 videos per week, with room for more work, higher pay and a long-term role if you perform well.



We are looking for someone who is serious about this opportunity and willing to commit. Please do not apply if you are looking to squeeze this in between many other jobs or cannot consistently deliver high-quality work.



TO APPLY

• A link to your portfolio website, Canva portfolio or similar professional portfolio
